newsitem.title: USA: WSCC approves raising Pacific Intertie capacity.
newsitem.headline: WSCC approves raising Pacific Intertie capacity.

text.p: Capacity of the Pacific Intertie power transmission system could increase by about 25 percent to 6,250 megawatts (MW) as early as Friday night, the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) said Friday.
Dennis Eyre, WSCC executive director, said "We advised the operator that the board members' endorsement is final."
The increase will remain in effect until April 30 or until criteria for the "winter" operating plan - such as load demand and hydropower generation - shifts to "spring" conditions.
Usage of the lines has been capped at 5,200 MW, out of a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, since last summer after the lines were involved in two widespread power blackouts across the western states.
A WSCC study group earlier this week delayed review of a spring operating plan amid concerns about whether direct power loads in southern California should be tripped off in an emergency.
The group will meet again April 9 to review the spring plan, which calls for raising the limit as high as 7,800 MW.
A final report on operating the system would then be due by April 20, with the WSCC board of trustees to vote on it April 24.

But concerns have been rasied that operating conditions on the Northwest hydroelectric system - mainly regional loads and the volume of power generation - will have changed so much by then that the winter plan might be obsolete.
If that were the case, the intertie capacity would revert to 5,200 MW until the spring plan is implemented.
